- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >73), model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline to 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from +0.27 to -0.16), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–2% per day for first 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1% upward bias to forecast mid-horizon to capture rebound.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overreact to recent highs; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
